The *Upādinnattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.28) is an Abhidhamma treatise forming part of the *Paṭṭhāna* collection in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. Structurally, it treats the analytical matrix combining the *upādinnattika* (triad of grasped or attached phenomena) and the *hetuduka* (dyad of root conditions) within the causal relational scheme of the Abhidhamma [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels are recorded by SuttaCentral, and no cross-language matches in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora are identified above threshold levels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus shows extensive internal reuse across the *Paṭṭhāna*, aligning 293 passages across 53 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The highest volume of shared phrasing occurs with *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 57 matches, with segment §1.1_0–3.1 aligned with §192.1_1–196.1), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1; 35 matches), and *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 15 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Further notable text reuse links it to neighboring combined treatments within the sixteenth division—such as *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 16.25), *Kusalattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.1), and *Vipākattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.27)—as well as other *Upādinnattika* sections (Patthana 19.4 and Patthana 13.4) [DharmaNexus].
